title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages): Sl(2,Z)^~ is the central extension of PSL(2,Z)=Sl(2,Z)/±1 by Z. It is the preimage of Sl(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R), i.e. the 'Teichmüller-type' group sitting over the modular group. Its lifted generators ρ̃, σ̃ satisfy ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2 = ω_0^{±1} (conditions (20) of the previous pages), and ω_0 generates the central kernel Z.

Theorem (25): Sl(2,Z)^~ = <ρ̃, σ̃ | ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2>.

Proof on this page:
- Let Π be the group defined by this presentation.
- Π → PSL(2,Z) = <ρ,σ | ρ^3 = σ^2 = 1> is surjective. Its kernel is the normal closure of ω_0 := ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2.
- ω_0 is central in Π (it commutes with both ρ̃ and σ̃), so its normal closure is just <ω_0>. This gives the exact sequence (27): Z → Π → PSL(2,Z) → 1.
- Π maps to the exact sequence 1 → Z → Sl(2,Z)^~ → PSL(2,Z) → 1, inducing identities on the end terms.
- The five lemma (here really the four lemma) shows Π ≅ Sl(2,Z)^~.

In modern terms, this is the identification of the lifted modular group with the braid group B_3, the trefoil knot group (and the mapping class group of the torus with one boundary component).

Corollary (28): Gl(2,Z)^~, the analogous Z-extension of PGL(2,Z), is the semidirect product B_3 ⋊ Z/2. It has presentation <ρ̃, σ̃, τ̃' | ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2, τ̃'^2 = 1, τ̃'ρ̃τ̃'^{-1} = ρ̃^{-1}, τ̃'σ̃τ̃'^{-1} = σ̃^{-1}>. Here τ̃' is the lift of an orientation-reversing involution acting by inversion on ω_0 (shown on the previous page).

Grothendieck then announces a second presentation by three involutive generators r̃_0, r̃_1, r̃_∞ lifting the three reflections r_0, r_1, r_∞ that generate PGL(2,Z), the (2,3,∞) triangle reflection group. On the next page this leads to an amalgam description of Gl(2,Z)^~.

Purpose: computing the 'Teichmüller groups' of the Longue Marche tower at the (1,1) level, together with their orientation-reversing (complex-conjugation) extensions, in explicit generators adapted to the Galois-action computations.
errors: No error in the argument on this page. The five lemma is applied to a top row not known to be left-exact. This is harmless: Z→Π composed with Π→Sl(2,Z)^~ equals the injective map Z→Sl(2,Z)^~, so Z→Π is injective; alternatively the four lemma suffices.
The boxed formula (28) is messy, with struck-out ω_0 and a dot. The intended relations are τ̃'^2 = 1 and ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2, not ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2 = 1.

Related issue on the next page, not this one: ρ̃ and σ̃ have infinite order in B_3. Hence the subgroups generated with τ̃' are infinite dihedral, and the labels D_6, D_8, D_4 cannot mean finite dihedral groups. They are either notation for the dihedral 'shape' or a slip.

ideas.what: Lifted modular group Sl(2,Z)^~ (central Z-extension of PSL(2,Z)) has presentation <ρ̃,σ̃ | ρ̃^3=σ̃^2>
ideas.modern_name: B_3 ≅ universal-cover preimage of SL(2,Z) in the universal cover of SL(2,R) ≅ trefoil knot group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Artin; trefoil group; Milnor's 'Introduction to Algebraic K-theory' / 'On the 3-dimensional Brieskorn manifolds')
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the Teichmüller tower at levels (0,4) and (1,1) but does not give this computation

ideas.what: Five-lemma argument using centrality of ω_0 to identify the normal closure with the cyclic subgroup
Presentation of the Z-extension of GL(2,Z) as B_3 ⋊ Z/2 with an involution inverting the generators; planned presentation by three involutions lifting the (2,3,∞) reflections
ideas.modern_name: extended braid group B_3^± / extended mapping class group of the once-bordered torus

deep.surprise_reason: Standard and correct identification of the lifted modular group with B_3 and of its extension by an inverting involution. It is useful as part of the Longue Marche bookkeeping of the Teichmüller tower with complex conjugation, but contains nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Boxed formula (28) should read: τ̃'^2 = 1, ρ̃^3 = σ̃^2, τ̃'(ρ̃) = ρ̃^{-1}, τ̃'(σ̃) = σ̃^{-1}. The ω_0 and the '·' are struck out.
'Gl(2,Z)^→' is probably Gl(2,Z) with a stray mark, or PGL(2,Z) = Gl(2,Z)/±1; the arrow reading is doubtful.
